newsitem.title: POLAND: Polish govt wants PLN 2.5 bln NBP borrowing limit.
newsitem.headline: Polish govt wants PLN 2.5 bln NBP borrowing limit.

text.p: The Polish government wants to amend this year's budget to get an additional 2.5 billion zloty ($739.6 million) borrowing limit from the central bank for flood relief, Prime Minister Wlodzimierz Ciomoszewicz said on Tuesday.

"I can say that even though the final version of the amendment has not yet been set, we will ask parliament to increase our borrowing limit in the National Bank of Poland (NBP) by 2.5 billion zlotys," Cimoszewicz told reporters.
The government will also seek an increase in its foreign borrowing limits to accomodate a $300 million loan from the World Bank, he said during a break in a cabinet meeting.
On Monday, Finance Minister Marek Belka said the government wanted to borrow more than one billion zlotys.
Cimoszewicz said the government did not discuss the option of a national borrowing scheme and ruled out a flood tax.
"We will not introduce the flood tax," Cimoszewicz said.

He stressed the increased borrowing limit in the central bank, which has yet to be approved by parliament at a special session on Wednesday, would not increase the budget deficit for 1997 and would act as bridge financing to ensure liquidity.
"The increase of the borrowing limit is to ensure temporary financing. It is not an additional 2.5 billion zlotys in the economy," Cimoszewicz said.
"Our intention is to keep the budget and macro-economic proportions set for this year. We do not want to increase spending but shift it so that certain expenditures are done ahead of time," he said.
Cimoszewicz said that by shifting funds within the existing budget the government had already managed to raise 650 million zlotys for the flood relief.

He said the government also empowered the finance ministry to set up a national lottery to raise money for dealing with the flood and to allot some of the revenue from existing lotteries for that purpose.

Cimoszewicz would not comment on the central bank's offer to lend the government up to one billion zlotys at commercial rates and collect deposits on the market to sterilise the monetary effect of the credit.
"This proposal has not been officialy presented to us," Cimoszewicz said.
